hunks.baseline: Jamukha stroked his beard as he watched a pale cloud of dust rise atop the distant cliffs, visible even in the darkness.
hunks.sol: Jamukha stroked his beard as he watched a pale cloud of dust rise from the distant cliff, visible even in the darkness.

hunks.baseline: No matter who he ran into up there, he would carry out his assigned task. And he would do it exceedingly well.
hunks.sol: No matter who he encountered up there, he would carry out his assigned task. And he would do it exceedingly well.

hunks.baseline: Flashes of light flickered without pause through the dust cloud, followed by more deafening crashes.
hunks.sol: Flashes flickered without pause through the dust cloud, followed by more deafening crashes.

hunks.baseline: Below, the nomads had shed their armor and taken up hooks and daggers. As the archers’ fire slackened, they seized the opportunity and rapidly climbed the cliffs.
hunks.sol: Below, nomads who had shed their armor and taken up hooks and daggers were climbing the cliffs as the archers’ fire slackened.

hunks.baseline: Arrows continued to fly, accompanied by occasional shouts, but that was all.
hunks.sol: Arrows still flew at the occasional shout, but that was all.

hunks.baseline: The archers’ composure and accuracy—and the dense crossfire pouring down from both sides—had faltered beyond comparison with what they’d been moments before.
hunks.sol: The archers’ composure and accuracy had faltered. So had the dense crossfire pouring down from either side. None of it compared to what it had been moments before.

hunks.baseline: Of the thousand archers holding the two cliffs facing each other, half had already been tied up by Chinggen. The other half also had to keep the ground forces in check as they surged into the gorge once more.
hunks.sol: Of the thousand archers holding the two cliffs facing each other, half were already tied up by Chinggen. The other half had to keep the ground forces in check as they surged into the gorge once more.

hunks.baseline: A net stretched thin would eventually tear.
hunks.sol: A loosened net would eventually tear.

hunks.baseline: The ten commanders of a hundred were outstanding leaders and fearsome warriors alike. For decades, they had been Jamukha’s most loyal servants.
hunks.sol: The ten commanders of a hundred were outstanding leaders and fearsome warriors alike. For decades, they had served Jamukha faithfully.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha watched them lead a hundred Keshik apiece, deflecting the arrows as they quickly began climbing the cliffs. Then he spoke again.
hunks.sol: Jamukha watched them lead a hundred Keshik apiece up the cliffs, deflecting arrows as they climbed. Then he spoke again.

hunks.baseline: “Your sworn brother’s killer is there.”
hunks.sol: “The man who killed your brother is there.”

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t just because they remembered their sworn brother, who had left days ago at the head of the vanguard with a hundred Keshik under his command, only for his head to return without him.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t simply that they remembered their sworn brother, who had left days ago at the head of the vanguard with a hundred Keshik under his command, only for his head to return without him.

hunks.baseline: It was pride.
hunks.sol: It was their pride.

hunks.baseline: Their lord was telling them to join forces and avenge the sworn brother who had died before them.
hunks.sol: Their lord was telling all three of them to join forces to avenge him.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha watched the three commanders step forward, one after the other.
hunks.sol: Jamukha watched the three commanders vie to step forward.

hunks.baseline: Their bulging temples and sharp, shining eyes showed that these masters had reached the upper reaches of the Peak realm.
hunks.sol: Their bulging temples and sharp, shining eyes showed that these masters had reached the far edge of the Peak realm.

hunks.baseline: But Jamukha was both their lord and their teacher.
hunks.sol: But Jamukha was both their lord and their teacher. He knew them better than anyone.

hunks.baseline: He knew them better than anyone.
A few days ago, his subordinate’s severed head had returned instead of news of victory. Jamukha had seen the wound on its neck, leaving him no choice but to make this decision.
hunks.sol: A few days ago, his subordinate’s head had returned instead of news of victory. Jamukha had seen the wound on its neck, leaving him no choice but to make this decision.

hunks.baseline: Send one man, and he wouldn’t return. Send two, and only one would make it back. Send three, and they would surely return with the man’s head.
hunks.sol: Send one man, and he would never return. Send two, and only one would make it back. Send three, and they would surely return with the man’s head.

hunks.baseline: That was why Jamukha’s resolve did not waver, despite the three commanders’ fighting spirit.
hunks.sol: That was why their eagerness to fight could not sway him.

hunks.baseline: Hundreds of figures shot across the gorge at speed, having left their horses behind. They clambered over the bodies of men and mounts, and over rocks.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of figures shot across the gorge, leaving their horses behind and vaulting over rocks and the bodies of fallen men and mounts.

hunks.baseline: Their first victims were not the Shanxi defenders, who continued to resist fiercely, but their own allies, stumbling backward in fear.
hunks.sol: Their first victims were not the Shanxi defenders, who continued to resist fiercely, but their own allies, backing away in fear.

hunks.baseline: Hundreds had joined the battle after the Great Steppe’s call to arms, but now the survivors of the small clan—reduced to half their original number—stared wide-eyed.
hunks.sol: Several hundred members of his small tribe had joined the battle at the Great Steppe’s call to arms. Now, reduced to half their original number, the survivors stared wide-eyed.

hunks.baseline: The Keshik slaughtered a hundred or so clansmen in moments with their lances and scimitars. The entire gorge froze at the sight.
hunks.sol: The Keshik slaughtered a hundred or so tribespeople in moments with their lances and scimitars. The entire gorge froze at the sight.

hunks.baseline: Temur’s voice shook as if he were caught in an earthquake.
hunks.sol: Temur’s voice shook as if the ground beneath him were quaking.

hunks.baseline: But the answer that came back, in both voice and gaze, was drier than the steppe’s bitter wind.
hunks.sol: But the voice and gaze that answered him were drier than the steppe’s bitter wind.

hunks.baseline: “They disobeyed the Khan’s orders and ordered a retreat on their own. We simply carried out the summary execution.”
hunks.sol: “They disobeyed the Khan’s orders and ordered a retreat on their own. They were executed on the spot.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. They’re your people, Khan Temur.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. They’re under your command, Khan Temur.”

hunks.baseline: A voice slipped between Jamukha’s lips, too quiet for anyone else to hear.
hunks.sol: Jamukha’s next words were too quiet for anyone else to hear.

hunks.baseline: “And the man who commands them is standing right beside me.”
hunks.sol: “And you, the man who commands them, are standing right beside me.”

hunks.baseline: Temur suddenly understood, under the pressure that felt like it was gripping his heart.
hunks.sol: Under a pressure that seemed to grip his heart, Temur suddenly understood.

hunks.baseline: The other man had drawn a line, and that was as far as Temur was allowed to go.
hunks.sol: This was the limit the man before him had set for him.

hunks.baseline: “N-no problem.”

hunks.baseline: At last, Jamukha nodded at the words Temur forced out through his fear and humiliation.
hunks.sol: Only when Temur had forced out those words through his fear and humiliation did Jamukha nod.

hunks.baseline: He had expected it when he begged for his life in front of Chinggen’s corpse, but had tried to look away. Now the terrible future he had feared was laid out before his eyes.

hunks.baseline: But as they died, those men would never know that the two young Great Chieftains who had brought them a brief peace and prosperity had already betrayed them.
hunks.sol: Yet as they died, those who had pledged loyalty and vengeance on the strength of a fabricated lie would never know that the two young Great Chieftains who had brought them a brief peace and prosperity had already betrayed them.

hunks.baseline: He had simply—

hunks.baseline: Leading twenty thousand clansmen who followed him and Chinggen into that dreadful gorge as arrow fodder, as human shields.
hunks.sol: Sending twenty thousand tribespeople who followed him and Chinggen ahead as arrow fodder, as human shields, to get through that dreadful gorge.

hunks.baseline: A figure approached at a run, accompanied by an urgent shout.
hunks.sol: A figure approached at a run, calling out urgently.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha recognized him as one of the Keshik who had headed into the gorge with the three commanders moments earlier. His gaze darkened at the sight of the weapons in the man’s hands.
hunks.sol: Jamukha recognized him as one of the Keshik who had headed into the gorge with the three commanders moments earlier. His gaze darkened.
More precisely, it darkened at the weapons in the man’s hands.

hunks.baseline: Even at a glance, the three weapons gave off a cutting edge far beyond that of anything the other nomads carried. They were familiar to Jamukha.
hunks.sol: Even at a glance, the three weapons had edges and points far keener than anything the other nomads carried. Jamukha knew them well.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha didn’t need to ask what fate had befallen their owners.
hunks.sol: He didn’t need to ask what fate had befallen their owners.

hunks.baseline: “Did those boys pass in peace?”
hunks.sol: “Did those boys go peacefully?”

hunks.baseline: The Keshik lowered the weapons that had become keepsakes and bowed his head.
hunks.sol: The Keshik set down the weapons, now keepsakes, and bowed his head.

hunks.baseline: “They fought bravely as warriors. Surely they’re now in Tengri’s embrace.”
hunks.sol: “They fought bravely as warriors. Surely they’ll be welcomed into Tengri’s embrace.”

hunks.baseline: That was the inescapable fate of a warrior of the Great Steppe.
hunks.sol: That was the inescapable fate of a warrior of the Great Steppe. The same fate awaited everyone else.

hunks.baseline: And it was the same for everyone else.
Everyone present already understood what he meant.
hunks.sol: Everyone present understood what he meant.

hunks.baseline: Even now, dozens of nomads were bleeding and falling somewhere in the gorge, but their lives were not part of any calculation.
hunks.sol: Even now, dozens of nomads were bleeding and falling somewhere in the gorge, but their lives counted for nothing in his calculations.

hunks.baseline: Three commanders had died, but their troops had suffered few losses. That could only mean one thing.
hunks.sol: Three commanders had died, but their troops had suffered few losses. That could mean only one thing.

hunks.baseline: Remembering the commanders’ confidence that each of them was enough on his own, Jamukha let out a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: Remembering how each commander had insisted he was enough on his own, Jamukha let out a quiet, incredulous laugh.

hunks.baseline: There was no doubt those three had fought a life-and-death duel.
hunks.sol: There was no doubt the three of them had fought life-and-death duels.

hunks.baseline: One after another.
hunks.sol: One at a time.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha silently looked down at the Keshik, who could only bow his head even lower rather than agree. Then, abruptly, he spoke.
hunks.sol: The Keshik could not bring himself to agree. Jamukha watched him bow his head still lower, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: “The senior ten-man commanders will temporarily take the vacant posts of commanders of a hundred. Minimize our losses as much as possible and wear them down.”
hunks.sol: “The senior ten-man commanders will temporarily fill the vacant posts. Keep losses to a minimum and wear the enemy down.”

hunks.baseline: He had no intention of wasting more strength in this narrow gorge—or of trusting the commanders who might do something foolish again at any moment.
hunks.sol: He had no intention of wasting more of his forces in this narrow gorge, or of trusting commanders who might do something foolish again.

hunks.baseline: He wanted a sure bet instead.
hunks.sol: He wanted a surer hand.

hunks.baseline: Not a fine steed or loyal hound that raced like the wind according to the direction of Jamukha’s reins, but a vicious dog that served the same master as he did.
hunks.sol: Not one of the fine steeds or loyal hounds that raced like the wind at the turn of his reins, but a vicious dog that served the same master he did.
